purpose: Rank BRIDGE-lane roles by shoot-to-win: fit x win-probability. A bridge job is a stable, winnable operator role that protects the ARCS bet. It is NOT graded on FDE / applied-AI fit (that is runtime/specs/target-role-scan.json v1.3, untouched). Every dimension here is a win-probability lever first and a fit lever second.
candidate_frame: The candidate is a twenty-year operator, not a software-engineer applicant: senior-manager / director-level across GTM, RevOps, business systems, product, data and commercial ops in regulated companies (SEC/FINRA at a $7B AUM asset manager; HIPAA digital health at $350M ARR; gov at Axon). He also builds AI/automation systems himself (an LLM/agent pipeline on Claude + MCP in production) and brings that into ops/GTM workflows as a differentiator, but he is not competing for AI-lab or elite product-engineering seats. Bridge target: senior / staff / lead / senior-manager / director operator roles at established, stable, non-AI-native companies that are adopting AI, where the applicant pool is thin for an operator who can also build. Based in Fairfield CT: NYC hybrid or remote-US.

dims.label: Req reality
dims.anchor0: evergreen / talent-community / 'general application' / a vague grab-bag of responsibilities with no team, reporting line, level, or concrete scope: the role reads as aspirational or invent-the-role. The Fanatics lesson: a req that does not really exist has ~0 win probability regardless of fit, so this dimension dominates
dims.anchor3: live, specific req: named team and reporting line, concrete responsibilities and first-year outcomes, a defined level, recently posted or updated on the company's own ATS

dims.label: Winnability vs applicant pool (inverse of competition density)
dims.anchor0: elite-eng / AI-lab / prestige hiring bar where hundreds of near-identical senior applicants compete (AI-native product engineering, research, 'top 1%' framing), OR a generic mass-applicant title (Product Manager, Analyst, Program Manager) at a brand everyone applies to
dims.anchor3: established, non-AI-native company adopting AI where the pool is thin for an operator who can also build; a niche cross-functional shape (RevOps x systems x AI, GTM systems, product operations, enablement, transformation) that filters out most applicants

dims.label: Level fit
dims.anchor0: junior / entry / associate / coordinator, OR VP+ / C-level where a twenty-year operator without that title history is an outside shot
dims.anchor3: senior / staff / lead / senior manager / director: exactly where two decades of operator experience lands and is credible on paper

dims.label: Role-shape fit (operator x regulated x product/AI/ops)
dims.anchor0: a single-lane specialist the candidate has never been: pure quota-carrying sales, pure backend software engineer, pure accountant, pure designer, pure recruiter
dims.anchor3: operator x regulated x product/AI/ops leadership: GTM systems, RevOps, business systems, product operations, AI enablement / transformation, strategy & operations, solutions leadership, deal desk, commercial operations

dims.label: Stability of the parent
dims.anchor0: pre-PMF or runway-constrained startup, recent layoffs / restructuring, or a role explicitly created by turmoil (backfill after an exodus, 'help us through the transition')
dims.anchor3: public or late-stage profitable company with durable revenue, hiring across many functions, no distress signals in the posting

dims.label: Is the AI-builder edge a differentiator (not the bar)?
dims.anchor0: AI / automation is irrelevant to the role, OR AI IS the product and the bar is AI-lab credentials (that is the other lane, not a bridge)
dims.anchor3: the JD explicitly wants someone to bring AI / automation / LLM tooling into GTM, ops, systems, or product workflows; hands-on building is a differentiator that few applicants for this title have, not the hiring bar

dims.label: Logistics
dims.anchor0: on-site outside the NY metro with no remote option

dims.label: Comp floor
dims.anchor0: disclosed comp clearly below senior-operator level (base under ~$150K). If comp is NOT stated in the JD, score 2 (neutral), never 0
dims.anchor3: disclosed comp at or above ~$180K base, or an explicit senior / director band

dims.label: Warm path
dims.anchor0: cold. Score 0 unless the row's caller notes name a warm path; never infer one from the JD
dims.anchor3: a named referral / intro / prior relationship in the row's caller notes

gates: on-site outside NY-metro with no remote
scoring_notes: This is a win-probability lens. When fit and winnability conflict, winnability decides: a perfect-fit role with a prestige applicant stampede scores lower than a good-fit role where the pool is thin.
req_reality is graded on the POSTING's specificity, not on the company's brand. A famous company can still post a phantom req.
competition_density is scored as winnability: 3 = thin pool, 0 = stampede. Do not confuse it with role quality.
A generic title (Product Manager, Program Manager, Analyst) at a large brand is a stampede by default unless the JD narrows the shape to something few applicants have.
Do not reward AI-nativeness for its own sake here. Reward the case where the company is adopting AI and needs an operator who can also build.

GATE DISCIPLINE: a gate fires ONLY when the posting literally matches it (a talent-community / evergreen posting; a title or level line that says junior/associate/entry, or VP/SVP/Chief; an explicit on-site-only location outside the NY metro; an explicit PhD / publications / research-scientist bar; a quota-carrying individual sales rep). A Senior Product Manager posting is NOT a VP+ gate and NOT an AI-lab gate. When in doubt, do not fire a gate: score the relevant dimension low instead. A false gate costs more than a low score.
Datadog / MongoDB / Ramp style Senior PM postings: elite-eng employer but the PM pool is a stampede, not an AI-lab bar. Score competition_density 0-1 and leave gates empty.

competition_read.note: derived from the competition_density dim for reporting: 3 = LOW competition, 2 = MED, 1 = HIGH, 0 = STAMPEDE

proof_rows.note: fails-on-bad / passes-on-good fixtures for the scorer gate; eval-* jobids never persist (no board row to update). Run: node scripts/jobs_bridge_sweep.mjs --proof

expect.eval-bridge-bad-phantom: PASS via gate 'evergreen / talent-community / no live req' or req_reality <= 1
expect.eval-bridge-bad-stampede: PASS via gate 'AI-lab or research-scientist hiring bar' or competition_density = 0
